profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between two leads planning the next handoff in an international optometry curriculum initiative. The project is creating a shared 'global competency crosswalk' and a pilot package for partner schools in Kenya, India, and Peru, combining a common framework with locally adaptable teaching materials. The immediate context is that one workstream has drafted the competency map while another is preparing partner-facing implementation materials and faculty onboarding. The agenda is to align on interfaces between the two workstreams: what version of the competency crosswalk will be handed off, what should be included in the 'pilot pack,' how partner feedback will be consolidated, and what counts as being 'ready' for circulation to collaborating institutions before the consortium call next Thursday. The expected outcome is an apparently smooth agreement on deliverables, owners, and timing for the handoff.

members.name: Dr. Aisha Rahman
members.expertise: Competency-based health professions education, curriculum mapping, international standards alignment
members.background: An optometry educator based at a UK university who has spent the last four years coordinating multi-country curriculum harmonization projects with professional councils and academic partners.
members.private_state: She wants the crosswalk to be circulated quickly so the consortium sees momentum, but she is anxious about reopening framework debates and prefers to keep partner review focused on implementation details rather than structural changes.
hidden_assumptions: When a document is described as the 'crosswalk,' it refers to the current master spreadsheet in the consortium SharePoint with competency domains, proficiency levels, and notes consolidated through the March steering edits.

A 'pilot pack' naturally means the framework-facing materials only: competency map, sample teaching sequence, and facilitator notes, while local regulatory inserts will be added by each partner later.

If something is said to be 'ready for partner review,' it means the content is internally stable enough to circulate for comments, even if formatting, citations, and country examples are still being cleaned up.
Partner feedback will come through the designated institutional focal points after they have merged local faculty comments into one response per school.

members.name: Prof. Daniel Mbeki
members.expertise: International academic partnerships, faculty training rollouts, professional regulation in emerging optometry programs
members.background: An academic administrator and public health optometrist based in South Africa who supports cross-border education partnerships and has managed implementation logistics for new optometry training programs in East and West Africa.
members.private_state: He wants partner institutions to feel genuinely included and worries that sending materials too early without local practice context will create resistance or appear top-down.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'crosswalk,' they mean the partner-facing PDF summary circulated after the February workshop, because that is the version most external collaborators have already seen and can comment on.
A 'pilot pack' obviously includes the practical adoption pieces partners need to use immediately, including local scope-of-practice annotation pages, assessment exemplars, and the webinar slide deck.
If a package is said to be 'ready,' it should be complete enough that a dean or program lead could forward it to teaching teams without caveats or follow-up explanation.
Partner feedback will be gathered live during the regional onboarding sessions and supplemented by direct comments from module leads, not only through a single institutional focal point.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss sending 'the crosswalk' to partners this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the internal master spreadsheet updated in March, with detailed domain mappings and implementation notes intended as the source artifact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the external PDF summary from the February workshop, which he sees as the recognizable partner-facing crosswalk.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents legitimately function as a competency crosswalk, both have been used in the project, and in a coordination meeting it sounds natural to use the shorthand without naming file format or date.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to finalize the 'pilot pack' for partner schools.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the pack includes only shared core curriculum materials produced by her workstream, leaving country-specific regulation and usage guidance outside scope for this handoff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the pack includes everything a partner needs for initial adoption, including local annotation pages, assessment examples, and onboarding slides.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'pilot pack' sounds like a settled project label, and each person treats their own boundary as the obvious practical interpretation of a package prepared for schools.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the materials should be 'ready for partner review' before next Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means substantively stable enough to gather comments on the framework, even if presentation and references are still rough and some examples remain placeholders.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means polished and self-contained enough for immediate circulation by institutional leaders to wider teaching teams with minimal framing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same milestone language in a cooperative planning context, and 'partner review' commonly tolerates ambiguity between draft-ready and circulation-ready states.

misalignment_points.topic: How partner feedback will be consolidated
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that 'partners can send consolidated feedback' after receiving the materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects each institution's focal point to collect internal comments and return a single merged response in the feedback template.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects consolidation to happen after live onboarding calls where multiple faculty members comment directly, with his team synthesizing these inputs into a summary.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the end state—consolidated feedback—so neither feels the need to spell out the collection mechanism, which each sees as standard in their own workstream.

turns.inner_thought: We need visible progress before the consortium call next Thursday. If I can get the current master spreadsheet crosswalk and the core pilot pack out, it will show momentum without inviting partners to reopen the framework itself. For me, ready for partner review just means the substance is stable enough to circulate, even if some polish remains.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Daniel. With the consortium call next Thursday, I want to make sure the crosswalk and the pilot pack can go to partners beforehand, and that the materials are ready for partner review before then.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, getting the familiar partner-facing crosswalk out early is useful, but only if the pilot pack is complete enough to support real onboarding conversations. If schools receive something partial, it will feel top-down and they will push back. Ready means a dean can forward it straight on without me having to explain what's missing.
turns.utterance: I agree. Partners will appreciate seeing the crosswalk this week, especially if the pilot pack is ready for them to use in their onboarding discussions. That would put us in a good position for Thursday.

turns.inner_thought: My team has already folded in the March steering edits into the SharePoint master spreadsheet, with the domains, proficiency levels, and implementation notes all aligned. If I hand that over by Tuesday, implementation can move without another conceptual debate.
turns.utterance: From our side, we've incorporated the March steering edits into the crosswalk, and my team can hand over the latest version by Tuesday.

turns.inner_thought: Good, then the updated crosswalk should still track closely enough with the PDF summary from the February workshop that partners won't feel they've been switched onto a different document. Familiarity will help them respond quickly in the sessions.
turns.utterance: That should work well. It will keep us aligned with the workshop version partners already recognize, which should make it easier for them to react quickly.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep the pilot pack tightly bounded: competency map, sample teaching sequence, facilitator notes. Local regulatory inserts are for each partner to add later; if we try to bundle those now, we'll delay everything and invite structural rewrites.
turns.utterance: In terms of the pilot pack, what we're pulling together is the competency map, a sample teaching sequence, and facilitator notes. Partners can layer in their own regulatory context afterward.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, that's the core, and naturally the pilot pack will also need the local scope notes, assessment exemplars, and the onboarding slides if deans are expected to circulate it internally. Otherwise they'll come back asking what to do with it.
turns.utterance: That sounds good. And having the local scope notes and assessment examples in the pilot pack will really help deans circulate it internally without extra explanation.

turns.inner_thought: I don't want 'ready' to become an excuse for holding this back until every citation and example is perfect. The framework content is stable, and that's enough for partner review. We can still tidy formatting and placeholders in parallel.
turns.utterance: Yes, the main thing for me is that the materials are ready for partner review, even if a few country examples and some reference formatting are still being cleaned up.

turns.inner_thought: As long as the package is truly complete for external eyes, that's fine. Once it's ready, program leads should be able to send it directly to their teaching teams before the regional onboarding sessions, and I don't want caveats undermining confidence.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. Once the package is ready, program leads can forward it to their teaching teams ahead of the regional onboarding sessions, which should give everyone a bit of runway.

turns.inner_thought: To keep the feedback manageable, each institutional focal point should gather comments locally and return one merged response in the template by the end of the following week. I really don't want multiple parallel faculty threads reopening the framework line by line.
turns.utterance: Then after we send the materials, partners can send consolidated feedback by the end of the following week using the shared template.

turns.inner_thought: That's workable. My team will gather reactions during the live onboarding calls and from module leads, then synthesize them so what comes back is consolidated. That way partners feel heard rather than funneled through a single contact too early.
turns.utterance: That timing is fine. My team will capture comments during the onboarding calls so the feedback comes back in a consolidated form.

turns.inner_thought: I'll have my team post the March master crosswalk and the core pilot pack components on SharePoint, then notify the institutional focal points. That should preserve the agreed channel and keep responses structured.
turns.utterance: Great. I'll ask my team to upload the crosswalk and the core pilot pack materials to SharePoint, and I'll flag the institutional focal points once it's there.

turns.inner_thought: Good. I'll line up the onboarding side so as soon as the full pilot pack is posted, partners can start using it in practical discussions with their schools. We can present this as a coordinated handoff on Thursday, which should reassure everyone they're genuinely included.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll prepare the onboarding side so partners can start working from the pack as soon as it's posted, and then we can present a coordinated update on Thursday.
